text:
sasha: Heads-up — spotted something weird in prod: v1->v2 header negotiation is causing duplicate quota hits for batched requests. cost spike in embedding jobs.

kevin: Oof. Can you repro? Is it only embeddings or gen too?

sasha: Mostly embeddings so far. Quick repro curl:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n  -H 'X-Api-Version: 2' \n  -d '{"model":"embed-large","inputs":["a","b","c"],"batch":true}'
```

sasha: In this case request goes to v1 endpoint but header kicks routing into v2 fallback path, and both routing layers increment request/usage counters (v1 counter + v2 fallback counter) so tenant gets double-billed for the same call.

nirav: I see matching traces — two route hops: primary v1 proxy and then v2-compatible handler. Telemetry shows both emitted meter events. Query I ran: grafana/dashboard/usage?q=tenant:acct-123&type=route_hits (link) — spike aligns with repro window.

taylor: Is the double-counting in our CDN proxy or in the internal metering shim? If it's at the proxy we might be able to stop emitting the second event on a fallback path.

kevin: Looks like metering happens in two places: request router (increments route_requests) and model-serving shard (increments model_invocations). For fallthrough routing we should be suppressing router-level model_invocations when we hand off. We added that suppression for streaming earlier but missed a code path for batched embeddings.

nirav: Also console shows quota alert emails going out which is bad. Tenant sees 2x usage and reaches quota thresholds prematurely. We should throttle alerts until we have fix.

sasha: Proposed short-term mitigations: 1) patch router to dedupe meter events for fallthrough paths (hotfix) 2) mute quota alerts for affected tenants for the last 12h while we validate backfill credits 3) add console flag to show "deduped" vs "raw" counts in usage UI.

taylor: Agree. For UX: in billing dashboard we can add an annotation for the window and a CTA to request credit. But long-term we should change routing semantics so only the final handler emits billing events.

kevin: Implementation note: add a request-scoped header X-Redwood-Meter-Handled=true when meter emitted so downstream won't double-count. Cheap and low-risk. We'll need to ensure header can't be spoofed by clients (strip inbound).

nirav: Also need telemetry: a new metric fallback_doublecount_rate and an alert if >0.5% of requests in a minute. Add a raw vs dedup delta graph to the routes page.

sasha: Can we canary the router patch to 5% first? Also we should backfill credits for the last 24h for tenants who hit quota because of this. I'll file a billing ticket.

console-bot: Deploy scheduled: routing-meter-dedupe -> canary 5% at 1744230000 ETA + smoke checks.

taylor: After canary, we should update the deprecation docs: clarify that X-Api-Version negotiation may cause fallthrough routing and that clients should prefer path+version alignment to avoid unexpected billing. Also add a console tip to detect mixed-version calls.

kevin: I'll own the patch (router + strip inbound header). Taylor, can you own the console flag and graphs? Sasha, you handle billing tickets and customer comms? Nirav, add telemetry query and alert.

sasha: Yep. I'll start drafting comms and a tenant credit spreadsheet.

nirav: Adding tickets now: GA-8942 (router patch), GA-8943 (console UI), GA-8944 (telemetry/alerts), GA-8945 (billing credits).

kevin: ETA for PR: today EOD. Can we coordinate a quick postmortem note after rollout? short bullet list: root cause, fix, tenant impact, credits issued.

sasha: Yes — let's keep it lightweight. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
